Propositions-as-Types Sort (Prop) & Two-Point Boolean Type (Bool)

Prop is the Curry-Howard sort of logical propositions in MKTD2-system (MKTD2-theory); Bool is the two-element Boolean data type with canonical inhabitants true (\mathsf{true}) and false (\mathsf{false}) used in conditional branching (Entries DefClassConditional (3.22)–DefDependentConditional (3.24)).

How to Understand It

How to Understand Prop and Bool (Unambiguous 3-Layer Distinction):

  • Fm (Syntactic Formulas in MKTD1-system / MKTD1-theory): Logical truth and falsity formulas are ⊤ : Fm (LaTeX \top, ASCII T) and ⊥ : Fm (LaTeX \bot, ASCII F), connected by formula implication —→ (LaTeX \longrightarrow, ASCII -->) and bi-implication ⟷ (LaTeX \longleftrightarrow, ASCII <-->).
  • Prop / Type (Constructive Types in MKTD2-system / MKTD2-theory): Unit and Void types are 𝟙 (LaTeX \mathbf{1} / \top, ASCII Unit) and 𝟘 (LaTeX \mathbf{0} / \bot, ASCII Void), connected by function space arrow → (LaTeX \rightarrow, ASCII ->) and type equivalence ↔ (LaTeX \leftrightarrow, ASCII <->).
  • Bool (Two-Point Computation Type in Entries DefClassConditional (3.22)–DefDependentConditional (3.24)): Inhabited by distinct boolean values true : Bool (LaTeX \mathsf{true}) and false : Bool (LaTeX \mathsf{false}), supporting both simple conditional branching (Entry DefSimpleConditional (3.23)) and dependent conditional branching if_dep over type families T_e : Bool → Type (Entry DefDependentConditional (3.24)).
